title: Eli Bitmap Font - Use bitmap fonts into your game!

posts.author: Eliaquim
posts.body:
Author: Hakuen Studio
​
Introduction
Those who want to use pixel fonts, or even more detailed fonts can get into a lot of trouble when aiming for the perfection of the font visuals.
Rpg Maker can blur and add an outline to your fonts. This plugin solves this problem, letting you use a bitmap font(a .png file) like a sprite sheet, which lets your fonts be rendered more faithful.
Features
• Add bitmap font to your game.
• Choose the size of the space between characters.
• Choose the size of the space
• Choose the characters(letters) your bitmap will use.
• Choose if you want to smooth or not the font.
• Can add as many fonts as you want. (PRO)
• Set specific fonts for scenes or windows. (PRO)
• Change text color. (PRO)
• Increase/decrease the font size (\{ \}) (PRO)
• Use Underline and Strike-through with Eli Message Actions. (PRO)

posts.body:
@magicbatteryacid
First, you need to set a
FontFace
(it works like an ID for the font inside the game). And in your screenshots, it is blank.
That problem is usually when the Bitmap font image width is not matching the number of characters * grid width.
Let's say you have 100 characters(letters) in your font.
When you create the PNG file, you have to create a grid for each character.
So, let's say the grid is 30x16.
So, each grid has 30 Pixels in width.
30*100 = 3000. That must be the width in your png file.
And 16 will be the height(size) of your font inside the game.
magicbatteryacid said:
Using the files in the sample project in our project, and trying to match up the settings, it wont display the text right. I even turned off every other plugin and it still has the same effect:
Click to expand...
The best way to make that is for you to open both projects, yours and the sample project.
Open the plugin manager on both.
Copy the BitmapFont on the plugin manager of the sample project and paste it into your project.
Copy all the bitmap font png files under the system folder from the sample project to yours.
And it should work.
But, if you try to manually copy each parameter, you can probably run into an issue or make some mistakes, like leaving the Font Face parameter blank.
But I suggest that instead of making the sample project settings work on your project, is better if you just try to build your own Bitmap Font Png File anyway.
Since if you tried the sample project, and it worked, then is probably a mistake while setting up the plugin on your project.
Create a blank project, only with Eli Book and Bitmap Font plugin.
Take any text editor, like notepad, and write down all the letters you will use in your game:
Now open your image editor(I use GIMP), create a larger canvas, and write down all those letters.
Now, figure out what is the largest letter and build the grid width size based on that. In my experience, it is always
W
or
M
.
Now, put every letter inside a grid.
Remember, the total width of the png file must be equal to the calculation:
Number of characters
*
Grid Width
Save the PNG file under the system folder.
Set the png file into the plugin parameter.
Copy the letters written on the notepad into the plugin parameters.
If the error persists, send the sample project you made and I will find the issue for you.

First off, the Font Face try not to use it as a number. Put a word there. Because if you set it as a number, the plugin may be confused you you are referencing a Font Face by it's ID or by it's Index.
And the Index, always starts at 0.
Meaning, if you have only two fonts on the plugin parameter. The first font Index is equal to 0. The second font index is equal to 1. And so on...
So if you set the Font Face/Index to 2 on the plugin command, but you only have two fonts on the plugin parameter(Index 0 and 1), the plugin will not find your font.
About the text picture plugin, I can't say about that. My recommendation is that first you manage to make the Bitmap Font plugin work as you want, on the default windows and menu of the RPG Maker.
